values.condition: Earlier literature measurement reported for comparison; consistent with the new measurement.

evidence.quote: Our measurement is consistent with the earlier found 1017 ± 2.7 km s−1, so we find no indication of binarity.

notes: S5-HVS1 is the only individually identifiable star retained. It was previously discovered/identified as an HVS candidate (T:p1-b5; T:p4-b9), and this paper's follow-up clearly identifies it as an HVS (T:p6-b4; T:p12-b12); the Fig. 7 caption places it in the predicted unbound-HVS population (I:p10-b0). I did not roster the 600 newly selected HVS candidates: although their implied-speed cut is described as ensuring unbound orbits (T:p3-b19), the final conclusion states all newly identified candidates were rejected (T:p14-b1), and only first-five catalogue/observational rows are supplied (T:p5-b0, T:p7-b0, T:p16-b1). The Brown et al. (2018) prior unbound candidates are discussed only as an unnamed seven-star group (T:p13-b2), so no individual IDs can be extracted.

S5-HVS1: The paper identifies S5-HVS1 as the previously discovered HVS but does not report its equatorial coordinates, parallax, proper motion, distance, galactocentric radius, Galactic rest-frame speed, or bound/unbound probability in the supplied text. Its position is only marked graphically in Fig. 7 without numerical values.
